raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`fused_mul_mat_gguf` sends standard and K-quant GGUF matmuls to MMQ (`ggml_mul_mat_a8`) for every batch larger than the MMVQ cutoff. MMQ's time grows linearly with the number of input rows. A prefill chunk has thousands of rows, so the GGUF linear layers become the bottleneck there.

The other option is to dequantize the weight once and run a dense bf16 GEMM, the path that I-Matrix types already take. That option has a mostly fixed cost, the dequantization, which even a small batch amortizes. Measured on an RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120) as the time per call of a 4096 x 2048 matrix, timed in CUDA graphs with weights cycled from DRAM:

| rows | Q4_K MMQ | Q4_K dequant + GEMM | Q6_K MMQ | Q6_K dequant + GEMM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.034 ms | 0.032 ms | 0.048 ms | 0.027 ms |
| 64 | 0.118 ms | 0.035 ms | 0.154 ms | 0.030 ms |
| 256 | 0.453 ms | 0.071 ms | 0.584 ms | 0.067 ms |
| 1024 | 1.82 ms | 0.22 ms | 2.31 ms | 0.22 ms |
| 4096 | 7.29 ms | 0.81 ms | 9.21 ms | 0.81 ms |
| 16384 | 29.1 ms | 2.96 ms | 36.8 ms | 2.96 ms |

At prefill sizes the dense path is about 10x faster.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py`:

- One module-level constant, `DEQUANT_MIN_ROWS = 16`.
- In `fused_mul_mat_gguf`, after the MMVQ branch, a batch of a `DEQUANT_TYPES` type with at least `DEQUANT_MIN_ROWS` rows goes through the existing `dequantize_gguf_weight` + `x @ weight.T` path.
- Smaller batches keep MMQ, and decode keeps MMVQ.

Crossovers on this GPU, over Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_0, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and Q8_0, 17 row counts from 16 to 16384, two passes in opposite order that pick the same winner in 357 of 357 cells:

| matrix | weights | dequant + GEMM as fast or faster from |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 x 1024 | 1M | 16-48 rows |
| 4096 x 2048 | 8M | 16-32 rows |
| 11008 x 4096 | 45M | 24-48 rows |

Summed slowdown over those cells, sum(chosen / best - 1): this rule (dense from 16 rows) 10.1, dense from 48 rows 25.3, the earlier version of this PR (48 rows and rows x weights >= 2^29) 160.3, MMQ throughout 1698.9. The earlier version's floor for small matrices came from eager per-call timing, which counted launch overhead and left small weights in L2; the review below found the same crossover on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (48 rows or fewer).

The dequantized weight is a transient bf16 tensor, the same as on the existing I-Matrix path.

## Accuracy Tests

The dense path does not quantize the activations to q8_1, so it is more accurate than MMQ. The table shows relative L2 error against an fp32 reference (fp32 activations @ fp32 dequantized weights), for a 4096 x 2048 matrix at 256 rows:

| type | MMQ | dequant + bf16 GEMM |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K | 6.0e-3 | 2.4e-3 |
| Q5_K | 5.9e-3 | 2.4e-3 |
| Q6_K | 5.6e-3 | 2.3e-3 |
| Q8_0 | 5.6e-3 | 1.7e-3 |
| Q4_0 | 1.0e-2 | 1.7e-3 |
| Q2_K | 5.6e-3 | 1.7e-3 |
| Q3_K | 5.6e-3 | 1.7e-3 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The kernel-level numbers are above. End to end, in our serving tree (SGLang with a KTransformers CPU/GPU hybrid MoE, so not upstream main itself), the same change took a 35K-token prefill of a GGUF model with Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K dense layers, TP2 on 2x RTX 5070 Ti, from 2,100 to 4,036-4,172 tok/s. That tree used a plain 64-row threshold.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit (ruff 0.15.1 format and the configured ruff rules).
- [ ] Add unit tests. This is a dispatch threshold on an existing path; the kernel-level benchmark and accuracy script can be added if useful.
- [ ] Update documentation (n/a).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

nodes.body: On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 188 SMs, 128 MiB L2), dense-after-dequant overtakes MMQ earlier than this rule switches in 20 of the 21 type and matrix groups. I timed both paths (sglang-kernel 0.4.10, rule from fdae9010f) in CUDA graphs with weights cycled from DRAM: 7 GGUF types, 1024x1024 to 11008x4096, 16 to 16384 rows, two passes in opposite order that pick the same winner in 356 of 357 cells. The crossover is at 48 rows or fewer (96 for Q2_K and Q4_0 at 1024x1024), but the rule waits for 512 rows on the 1M-weight matrix, so its summed slowdown, sum(chosen/best - 1), is 118.9 (118.3 and 119.6 per pass), mostly there; always taking the dense path scores 6.7. The weights were synthetic GGUF blocks, so this is timing only.

Thanks, this reproduces on an RTX 5070 Ti (SM120, 70 SMs, 48 MiB L2). I used sglang-kernel 0.4.10, CUDA graphs, weights cycled from DRAM, and the same 7 types × 3 matrices × 17 row counts in two passes of opposite order. The passes agree in 357 of 357 cells.

Dense-after-dequant is as fast or faster from 16–48 rows in every group, the 1M-weight matrix included. Summed slowdown, sum(chosen/best − 1), for each rule:

| rule | score |
|---|---|
| this PR's rule (before) | 160.3 |
| rows ≥ 48 alone | 25.3 |
| always dense | 10.1 |
| always MMQ | 1698.9 |

The 192–512-row crossovers in the description came from eager per-call timing over four weight copies. That timing counted launch overhead, and it left the 1M-weight matrices in L2. 0c7089b drops `DEQUANT_MIN_WORK` and switches at 16 rows (the smallest count either of us measured; below that the MMVQ / MMQ choice stays as it is). I also corrected the description.

A note for later: with llama.cpp's int8 tensor-core MMQ from #43650, the result reverses on the same card and grid. Always-MMQ scores 33.8 and always-dense 224.4, and dense only wins on the 1M-weight matrix and on Q2_K / Q3_K / Q6_K at large row counts. Once #43650 lands, this rule should become a per-type exception instead of a row count.

@@ -178,6 +178,13 @@ def is_layer_skipped_gguf(prefix: str, modules_to_not_convert: list[str]):
 DEQUANT_TYPES = STANDARD_QUANT_TYPES | KQUANT_TYPES | IMATRIX_QUANT_TYPES
 MMVQ_QUANT_TYPES = STANDARD_QUANT_TYPES | KQUANT_TYPES | IMATRIX_QUANT_TYPES
 MMQ_QUANT_TYPES = STANDARD_QUANT_TYPES | KQUANT_TYPES
+# ggml_mul_mat_a8 (MMQ, dp4a) grows linearly with the number of input rows, while
+# dequantizing the weight once and running a bf16/fp16 GEMM has a mostly fixed cost
+# (the dequant) that a small batch already amortizes. Timed in CUDA graphs with weights
+# from DRAM over Q2_K..Q8_0 and matrices of 1M-45M weights, the GEMM path is as fast or
+# faster from 16-48 rows on an RTX 5070 Ti and from 48 rows or fewer (96 in two small
+# cases) on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell; at prefill sizes (thousands of rows) ~10x faster.
+DEQUANT_MIN_ROWS = 16
 
 
 def dequantize_gguf_weight(
@@ -206,6 +213,10 @@ def fused_mul_mat_gguf(
     # enable MMVQ in contiguous batching with batch_size=1
     if x.shape[0] <= mmvq_safe and qweight_type in MMVQ_QUANT_TYPES:
         y = ggml_mul_mat_vec_a8(qweight, x, qweight_type, qweight.shape[0])
+    # Large batches (prefill): dequantize once and use a dense GEMM
+    elif x.shape[0] >= DEQUANT_MIN_ROWS and qweight_type in DEQUANT_TYPES:
+        weight = dequantize_gguf_weight(qweight, qweight_type, x.dtype)
+        y = x @ weight.T
     # Use MMQ Kernel if it's available (standard + k-quants)
     elif qweight_type in MMQ_QUANT_TYPES:
         y = ggml_mul_mat_a8(qweight, x, qweight_type, qweight.shape[0])
